messages.author: a8334d46c5367a85
messages.subject: orderMarkers() Vs. Physical position
parts:
Dr. Broman,

I created a linkage map from a F2 population genotyped by WGS.
If I use physical position for marker ordering, then the map length looks good and the results seems ok but the issue is the population I used is quite different from the reference genome in which the alignment was performed.
I want to point out few regions of conflict between reference and my population even at the risk of inflating the map a bit.
So, I tried to order markers without the use of physical position and the initial order given by orderMarkers(mapthis, chr=1, use.ripple = FALSE) doesnot look that good and without use.ripple=FALSE, it doesn't even give me results for the markers I have (~2500).

To infer order, I then used the codes below like you suggested in one of the questions asked here.
rip2 <- ripple(mapthis, chr=1, window=3)
summary(rip2)
rip5lik <- ripple(mapthis, chr=1, window=3, method="likelihood", error.prob=0.005)
summary(rip5lik)

rip5lik is taking a lot of time even at window size of 3 and looks like the order isn't as accurate.
Is there a way to order markers by physical position and still look for signs of inversions or rearrangement in R/qtl?

Thanks,

Prashant

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] orderMarkers() Vs. Physical position
parts:
I would start with the physical order rather than try to reorder markers from scratch. 

The likelihood method is going to be super slow, because for each marker order it is attempting to re-estimate inter-marker distances for the full chromosome. Using crossover counts is much faster.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] orderMarkers() Vs. Physical position
parts:
Hi Karl,

To add onto this, as suggested in a previous discussion. I started with the physical positions, assuming these are correct (converting the physical position to cM by dividing by 1,000,000).

I am working with maternal markers (backcross, AB x AA) from an outbred population.  I see significantly inflated estimates of map sizes.  So far, I have gone through several iterations of rippling using increases window sizes (3,4,5, etc.) and at each window, repeat the cycle until no new XOs are identified with that window size before moving up.  I am seeing incremental changes but still have significantly inflated map sizes.

I'm wondering if there is a way to format the for loop to iterate over a list of increasing window sizes and then move onto a new window size when no improvements are found? Additionally, would there be a way to record how many iterations were needed at each window size interval (i.e. append the results from each iteration to a file that was stored separately from the ripple results)?

I've adapted the code from the book (pgs.60-66) and have it included here:

rip <- vector("list", nchr(fake.qtl))
names(rip) <- names(fake.qtl$geno)

for ( i in names(fake.qtl$geno))
  rip[[i]] <- ripple(fake.qtl, i, 7, method = "countxo")

dif.nxo <- sapply(rip, function(a) a[1, ncol(a)] - a[2,ncol(a)])
dif.nxo

for ( i in names(fake.qtl$geno)) {
  if(dif.nxo[i] > 0)
    fake.qtl <- switch.order(fake.qtl, i, rip[[i]][2,])
}

It would greatly help to automate this process and also be able to review the output after the fact to identify areas that were potentially problematic for ordering, etc.

Thanks,
Josh
